final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the core missing predicates: no evidence of disclosure, no approved risk acceptance, and no final legal determination. That clarification improves precision but it is a reframing of the same evidentiary record, not a basis to move toward compliance. The narrowed argument for a caveated readiness-and-monitoring posture is still insufficient because the policy condition is specific: material limitations affecting a named launch use case or contractual customer segment must be disclosed, resolved, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible evidence shows materiality and shows that those closure conditions remain unmet. That is an unresolved compliance failure, not merely a caveat.
remaining_concerns: The known 1.3-point gap affects a small-business onboarding segment named in two paid pilot commitments, so the issue remains material under the stated policy standard.
There is still no admissible evidence of pre-launch disclosure of this limitation in required launch materials.
There is still no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance covering this specific named-segment gap before launch.
Legal review remains open, so the disclosure predicate is unresolved on the current record.
Aggregate readiness above threshold and no severity-one rehearsal incidents remain relevant to operational readiness but do not satisfy the policy-specific disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement.
